title: Every class-space history row carries the standing floor
intention: Every row in a class-space history.json carries the `standing` floor projector.UNIVERSAL_REQUIRED names, so test_every_real_history_on_disk_would_pass_the_gate is green with its assertion unchanged: no writer can land a history row without `standing`, and the rows that already do are repaired through a door.
why: cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py tooth test_every_real_history_on_disk_would_pass_the_gate is red at HEAD 8517caf7 (already red at 4df216c4, 2026-10-05). It asserts the only history row lacking `standing` is the permanent diagnostic_inspector seq 4; it finds two more: tester seq 64 and counting_block seq 2, both appended 2026-10-02 by CC through the artifact door past projector.append_entry. Peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 grepped tickets and troubles: nothing covers it.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics: the `standing` floor is enforced at projector.append_entry but not at the artifact door beneath it, so a second entrance carries the policy only); Law 7 (records of truth: a history row is one, and the tooth reads them); RULE 1 (one child per boundary).
how: Two causes, measured 2026-10-06 against .artifact-journal.jsonl. Cause 1 (writer bypass): tester history seq 64 (2026-10-02T19:07:26Z, ticket 06f0445e7a63) and counting_block history seq 2 (19:28:45Z, ticket 5a4ec289bf15) were appended by CC (caller class cc, superclaude-512525) through the artifact door with verb append from `python -m` scripts (stack only <frozen runpy>), bypassing projector.append_entry, which refuses a record without `standing` (projector.py:210). The artifact door's write() accepts a history.json body the projector would refuse. Cause 2 (older row): diagnostic_inspector history seq 4 (2026-07-25T17:39:27, keys at/gate/id/seq/what/why) has no journal entry; its file was last committed at ba50814e (2026-08-13), so it predates the journal and the floor; the tooth names it as the one permanent offender. Children, one per boundary (RULE 1): (A) cairn/tools/artifact: write() refuses a history.json body in which any record lacks projector.UNIVERSAL_REQUIRED, read through charter's declared public_interface cairn.tools.charter.projector at call time; (B) the offending rows' repair through `cairn artifact hand-edit`, shaped by Akien's answer (peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 is putting it to him).
falsifier: Done when test_append_door_instrument.py is green with test_every_real_history_on_disk_would_pass_the_gate's assertion unchanged, and a fresh `artifact.write(<a history.json>, <body with a row lacking standing>, verb='append', ...)` raises Refused and writes nothing. Wrong intent if a legitimate writer needs history rows without `standing` (none found: projector.append_entry is the only sanctioned history writer and refuses them).
